title: Tower Bridge
blurb: London’s Grade I listed combined bascule and suspension bridge over the Thames, in simplified schematic form: two 213 ft towers, two 1,070-ton bascules, high-level walkways and 270 ft suspension side spans.

systems.name: Substructure
systems.description: The two 185 ft by 70 ft concrete piers in the Thames and the shore abutments with their smaller towers.

systems.name: Towers
systems.description: The two 213 ft steel-framed towers in Cornish granite and Portland stone, crowned with Gothic pinnacles.

systems.name: Bascules
systems.description: The two counterbalanced leaves of the 200 ft opening span, each about 1,070 tons, with counterweights and pivots.

systems.name: High-level walkways
systems.description: The pedestrian walkways 143 ft above high water, with glass floors fitted in 2014.

systems.name: Suspension side spans
systems.description: The two 270 ft suspension side spans: decks, chains, suspenders and abutment anchorages.

systems.name: Roadway and footways
systems.description: The low-level deck: roadway, footways passing around the towers, and parapets.

systems.name: Hydraulic machinery
systems.description: The steam-driven hydraulic plant that raises the bascules, and the Victorian engine room.

explanations.north pier: One of two piers sunk into the Thames riverbed to carry the bridge, each stipulated by the 1885 act to be 185 ft long and 70 ft wide. Together the piers hold over 70,000 long tons of concrete. Exact outline is schematic.
explanations.south pier: One of two piers sunk into the Thames riverbed to carry the bridge, each stipulated by the 1885 act to be 185 ft long and 70 ft wide. Together the piers hold over 70,000 long tons of concrete. Exact outline is schematic.
explanations.north abutment: The north shore abutment at Tower Hill, with its smaller tower, anchoring the suspension chains. The bridge is 940 ft long including the abutments. Exact outline is schematic.
explanations.south abutment: The south shore abutment at Bermondsey, with its smaller tower, anchoring the suspension chains. The bridge is 940 ft long including the abutments. Exact outline is schematic.
explanations.north tower: The north tower: a steel skeleton faced in Cornish granite and Portland stone in Victorian Gothic style, rising 213 ft. The roadway passes through it while the footways pass around it. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.south tower: The south tower: a steel skeleton faced in Cornish granite and Portland stone in Victorian Gothic style, rising 213 ft. The roadway passes through it while the footways pass around it. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.north tower pinnacles: Four Gothic pinnacles crowning the north tower, the signature silhouette that makes the bridge read as a medieval gatehouse. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.south tower pinnacles: Four Gothic pinnacles crowning the south tower, the signature silhouette that makes the bridge read as a medieval gatehouse. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.north tower steel columns: Four octagonal steel columns, each 119 ft 6 in long, one at each corner of the north tower: the structural skeleton inside the stone facing. Positions are schematic.
explanations.south tower steel columns: Four octagonal steel columns, each 119 ft 6 in long, one at each corner of the south tower: the structural skeleton inside the stone facing. Positions are schematic.
explanations.north bascule leaf: The north leaf of the opening span: four steel girders carrying the roadway plate, projecting 100 ft toward the opposite tower when lowered. Each leaf weighs about 1,070 tons including ballast and paving. Exact girder shapes are schematic.
explanations.south bascule leaf: The south leaf of the opening span: four steel girders carrying the roadway plate, projecting 100 ft toward the opposite tower when lowered. Each leaf weighs about 1,070 tons including ballast and paving. Exact girder shapes are schematic.
explanations.north bascule counterweight: The ballasted tail of the north leaf, extending back into the pier to counterbalance the projecting section so the leaf can be raised with little force. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.south bascule counterweight: The ballasted tail of the south leaf, extending back into the pier to counterbalance the projecting section so the leaf can be raised with little force. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.bascule pivots: The 25-ton solid steel pivots on which the leaves turn, each 1 ft 9 in in diameter and 48 ft long, set 13 ft 3 in inside the pier faces and 5 ft 7 in below the roadway. Exact positions are schematic.
explanations.west high-level walkway: The west pedestrian walkway 143 ft above high water, spanning the 200 ft between the towers so foot traffic could continue while the bascules were raised. Closed in 1910, reopened in 1982 as exhibition space. Exact tube profile is schematic.
explanations.east high-level walkway: The east pedestrian walkway 143 ft above high water, spanning the 200 ft between the towers so foot traffic could continue while the bascules were raised. Closed in 1910, reopened in 1982 as exhibition space. Exact tube profile is schematic.
explanations.walkway glass floors: Glass floor panels fitted in both walkways in 2014, letting visitors look straight down at the road and the Thames 143 ft below. Exact panel layout is schematic.
explanations.walkway roofs: The roofs of the two walkway tubes. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.north suspension side deck: The deck of the north 270 ft suspension side span, from the abutment to the north tower. Exact deck depth is schematic.
explanations.south suspension side deck: The deck of the south 270 ft suspension side span, from the abutment to the south tower. Exact deck depth is schematic.
explanations.north suspension chains: The suspension chains of the north side span, anchored at the abutment and rising to the north tower. Exact chain curve is schematic.
explanations.south suspension chains: The suspension chains of the south side span, anchored at the abutment and rising to the south tower. Exact chain curve is schematic.
explanations.north suspension suspenders: Vertical suspender rods hanging the north side-span deck from its chains. Exact spacing is schematic.
explanations.south suspension suspenders: Vertical suspender rods hanging the south side-span deck from its chains. Exact spacing is schematic.
explanations.chain anchorages: Anchorage blocks at both abutments where the suspension rods are made fast, tied back through rods contained within the upper walkways. Exact block shapes are schematic.
explanations.roadway: The A100 roadway across the bridge, part of the London Inner Ring Road carrying about 40,000 crossings a day. Exact surfacing is schematic.
explanations.low-level footways: The low-level pedestrian footways, passing around the outside of the towers while the roadway passes through them, and jogging outward at each tower. Exact alignment is schematic.
explanations.parapets: Parapets along the deck and approach stubs, 60 ft apart between parapets across the side spans. Exact railing pattern is schematic.
explanations.hydraulic accumulators: The six hydraulic accumulators storing pressurised water at 750 psi under very heavy weights on 20-inch rams, the stored energy that raises the bascules. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.steam pumping engines: The stationary steam engines driving the force pumps for the accumulators: pairs of larger 8 1/2 in and smaller 7 1/2 in three-cylinder engines, with redundancy built in. Exact engine shapes are schematic.
explanations.victorian engine room: The Victorian engine rooms in a separate building near the south end of the bridge, housing the original steam engines as part of the Tower Bridge Exhibition. Exact building shape is schematic.
